title: Localizing near a glancing ray: two scales and the normal derivative
reviewed_arguments: The derivative lemma needs only a continuous real field and C1 functions. It differentiates the smooth localization before estimating its support and never differentiates a fourth root.

All three parameter powers and constants are explicit: A squared times delta, AB times delta/epsilon and A to the three-halves times its square root. Each threshold costs at most c/6, giving c/2. The zero derivative constant case is separate.

Compatible positive widths, the order of their choice and every real-power example retain epsilon at most one after shrinking delta. Independent vanishing of the widths does not imply the needed ratio bound.

The full degree-two Hamilton field retains its normal momentum derivative, has nonzero tangential covector and an invariant unit-momentum slice. Its characteristic equation is x=rho squared and the double normal derivative has the positive stated value.

At the positive normal root the exact localized derivative is 1-2sqrt(delta/epsilon), with threshold 1/16. The opposite root reverses only the normal contribution, giving 1+2sqrt(delta/epsilon). Superlinear epsilon decay destroys the desired sign while the points remain on the same smooth characteristic model.

The mixed estimate applies to an arbitrary complex Hilbert space and to the specified domain vector of an otherwise unbounded linear A. R is bounded; no self-adjointness or separability assumption is used. CE:H5 contains the complete pointwise Cauchy–Schwarz proof BI13a, explicitly selected here.

The norm square is converted to a norm before Cauchy–Schwarz. The exact nonnegative-square proof of Young supplies the displayed epsilon-dependent remainder. The additional mixed error is treated by the same full inequality.
Absorption retains the full coefficient 2M squared divided by beta squared epsilon squared, treats zero M or K, and requires a separate uniform PDE estimate for the remainder in later applications.

The scalar example realizes the square-root order exactly and disproves a uniform delta bound. Both complete exercises retain their precise thresholds, locality constraints and explicit remainder warning.

The original mathematical body agrees with the historical staged version. All 22 obligations and 18 displays are preserved. The exact two-panel diagram uses rationally checked quadratic parametrizations and explicitly different vertical scales.
later_scope_not_claimed: Full microlocal normal-energy inequality and exact source/Sobolev remainder
